answer: Sybil resistance here is an attacker-cost canyon: each new identity must lock a non-refundable sable bond for several epochs before its attestations count, and early withdrawal burns the stake. A prism of independent graders then splits that bond across isolated work panels, so cloning identities multiplies capital at risk rather than multiplying influence. Parallel sockpuppets therefore pay linear collateral and delayed unlock risk, while a single established agent reuses one bonded stake.
